strings.name: Kim Jong Un
strings.summary: Kim Jong Il’s son studied in Switzerland and assumed North Korea’s supreme power after his father’s death in 2011, consolidating party, state and military posts. He expanded nuclear and missile programmes, held talks with South Korean and US leaders, then deepened Russian security ties. His rule involves severe social control and international human-rights criticism. His birth year is unconfirmed: sources give 1982, 1983 or 1984.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Long leads North Korea; his nuclear, missile and foreign-relations policies significantly affect the Korean Peninsula and international security.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: North Korea; birth year unconfirmed, with sources giving 1982, 1983 or 1984.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Reported schooling near Bern, Switzerland, followed by university and military education in North Korea.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Nuclear and security policy
strings.highlights.h1.text: Expanded nuclear and missile capabilities, strongly affecting peninsula security.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Summits and alliances
strings.highlights.h2.text: Held talks with US leadership, then strengthened Russian security cooperation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Reelected party general secretary
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Workers’ Party’s ninth congress reelected him general secretary.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Russia–North Korea treaty
strings.timeline.t2.text: Signed a comprehensive strategic partnership treaty with Putin including mutual defence.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Singapore summit
strings.timeline.t3.text: First met US President Trump to discuss relations and denuclearisation.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Sixth nuclear test
strings.timeline.t4.text: North Korea conducted its sixth test, prompting international condemnation and sanctions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: State Affairs Commission
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became chairman of the newly established state body.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Party leadership post
strings.timeline.t6.text: Elected Workers’ Party first secretary, further consolidating power.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Assumed supreme power
strings.timeline.t7.text: Named successor after Kim Jong Il’s death, then supreme military commander.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Schooling in Switzerland
strings.timeline.t8.text: Reporting links him to schooling near Bern from 1998 to 2000.
